claim.why_it_matters: The column's first twelve lines lose the index hierarchy: sub-entries and headwords are printed at the same level, so 'SET statement, attribute setting 574' reads as a top-level entry. The index is informative, but a flattened or merged index entry misattributes page references to the wrong headword.

verdict.reasoning: The rendered page (printed folio 905) shows the left column's first twelve lines at two levels. 'WRITE statement 619', 'SET statement, attribute setting 574', 'LOCK MODE clause 259', 'DEFAULT ROUNDED clause 219' and 'ROUNDED phrase 447' are indented sub-entries. 'ATAN function 646', 'ATTRIBUTE phrase', 'AUTO clause 299', 'Automatic data 134, 432', 'Automatic items 134', 'AUTOMATIC phrase' and 'AWAY-FROM-ZERO phrase' are flush headwords. In page-929.md, all twelve lines carry the same three leading spaces. Markdown strips that indent, so every line renders at one level. The rest of the same page marks sub-entries with   (for example 'Based data item 419' / ' ALLOCATE statement 470'), so this block breaks the transcription's own convention. Nothing is missing and nothing is misquoted: the text matches word for word. The only difference is the lost nesting, which detaches four sub-entries from their headwords (ATTRIBUTE phrase, AUTOMATIC phrase, AWAY-FROM-ZERO phrase). That is a real structural defect in an informative index. It is not normative.
verdict.corrected_description: Lost indentation, not misplaced content. On p929 (printed 905), the transcription gives the first twelve left-column index lines the same three-space indent instead of the   sub-entry marker the rest of the page uses. As a result, the sub-entries 'WRITE statement 619' (continued from the previous page), 'SET statement, attribute setting 574' (under ATTRIBUTE phrase), 'LOCK MODE clause 259' (under AUTOMATIC phrase), and 'DEFAULT ROUNDED clause 219' and 'ROUNDED phrase 447' (under AWAY-FROM-ZERO phrase) render at the same level as the headwords. The fix is to prefix those five lines with   and strip the leading spaces from the seven headword lines. The text itself is complete and correct. Severity: structural (informative index).
